title: Call serialization glitch — logbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal log for the next 48–72h while chasing a recurring serialization/parsing failure when invoking external tools via tool-calls (user-facing function/tool call flow). Not an official incident writeup — working notes and experiments, keep ephemeral.

Context summary (short):
- Symptoms: ~0.3% of production tool-call responses contain malformed JSON payloads (extra control chars, truncated arrays) that the structured-output validator rejects. This leads to a cascade: fallback => secondary model route => higher latency + token waste.
- Surface area: hosted API + dedicated capacity; reproduced locally using same model weights + sanitized traffic replay.
- Hypothesis: either (A) serialization on the runtime side sometimes truncates at buffer boundary, (B) streaming chunk assembly loses a boundary/escape sequence, or (C) a model tokenization/emit oddity for certain prompt prefixes.

Repro steps and commands I ran (workstation):
1) Simple replay harness (python):
   PYTHONPATH=./tools python tools/replay_toolcall.py --trace-id TRACE-20260220-0811 --output debug/replay-TRACE-0811.json --model rwd-7b --retries 1
   Observed: ~2 failures in 2000 requests (matches ~0.1%–0.3%). Failures saved in debug/failures/trace-0811-*.json

2) Run validator locally against saved payloads:
   cat debug/failures/trace-0811-0003.json | jq -r .tool_output > tmp/out.txt
   python tools/validate_structured_output.py tmp/out.txt --schema tools/schemas/tool-response-v2.json --verbose
   Error: JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 384 (char 383)

3) Attempt re-assembly of streaming chunks (simulate):
   # script used to replay chunk stream
   python tools/reassemble_stream.py debug/streams/stream-0811.log --trace 0003 --out tmp/reassembled.json
   Diff between saved stream and final payload: extra byte 0x1E before array start in problematic cases.

Representative error snippets (raw bytes shown as hex where helpful):
- Validator output (problematic payload excerpt):
  ... "items": [
  "id": 243,
  0x1E
  "metadata": {
    "name": "transform-step"

- Python stack when json.loads fails:
  File "/venv/lib/python3.11/json/__init__.py", line 293, in loads
    return _default_decoder.decode(s)
  File "/venv/lib/python3.11/json/decoder.py", line 337, in decode
    obj, end = self.raw_decode(s, idx=_w(s, 0).end())
  json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 384 (char 383)

Early observations / patterns: (keep updating)
- Control character 0x1E (record separator) appears in ~85% of failures; sometimes 0x0F shows up in others.
- Failures correlate with payloads that include long arrays (~>~150 items) and when the model emits many small tokens vs a few long tokens (i.e., tokenization pattern matters).
- Failures appear both in streaming and non-streaming paths, but streaming path has higher incidence.
- Not bounded to a specific model family — reproduced with rwd-7b and rwd-13b-quant.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Chunk assembly bug: a trimming/concat step treats 0x1E as delimiter and sometimes drops the separator but leaves the byte in the payload stream, producing invalid JSON. (High plausibility given 0x1E)
2) Encoder mismatch: some component encodes bytes as latin-1 in one step then UTF-8 elsewhere, producing stray control bytes when reinterpreted.
3) Model token emission: certain tokens map to bytes that include unescaped control characters; earlier sanitizers remove them but edge case let slip through. (Lower — model outputs should be text)

Experiments and results so far:
A) Force strict UTF-8 sanitization in the serving runtime (local build):
   - Patch: runtime/streaming/assemble.cpp -> sanitize_control_chars(buffer) before append.
   - Rerun replay (same trace): failures dropped 90% (from 2 to 0 in smaller run), but one failure still present and was different (0x0F).
   - Conclusion: sanitization helps but not a full fix.

B) Add logging on chunk boundaries to include chunk length and source (kernel vs user) in production canary (small traffic slice):
   - Added: trace tags, chunk_id, chunk_len, prev_last_byte.
   - Observed: in failing traces, previous chunk last_byte == 0xC3 and next chunk first_byte == 0x9E producing combined 0xC39E -> interpreted differently if encoding mishandled.
   - Suggests encoding coupling issue (hypothesis 2) still plausible.

C) Replace stream concat logic to copy into a single buffer (avoid multiple appends) to test race/partial-write possibility:
   - Local test run: no failures seen in 10k synthetic requests. But this test uses synthetic payloads (no model in the loop).

Tools & quick scripts (inventory):
- tools/replay_toolcall.py (python) — replays recorded traces with model or canned responses.
- tools/validate_structured_output.py (python) — strict schema validator using jsonschema + custom checks.
- tools/reassemble_stream.py (python) — reconstructs stream sidecars into final payload for diff.
- runtime/streaming/assemble.cpp — primary assembly code in C++ serving runtime.

Immediate next steps (short list):
- [ ] Push a small, reversible runtime patch that: (1) logs raw chunk bytes (hex) for failing traces only, (2) applies conservative sanitization (strip ascii control <= 0x1F except 
      	tab/newline/carriage return). Coordinate with SRE for limited canary. (Priority: High)
- [ ] Add a stage in the validator to show hex dump on parse error and include last ~256 bytes to surface boundary artifacts. (Priority: High)
- [ ] Run controlled experiment with variant tokenizers (force different tokenization granularity) to see correlation. (Priority: Medium)
- [ ] Re-run synthetic test where model + runtime are in the loop but inputs crafted to trigger many small-token emissions. (Priority: Medium)
- [ ] If logging shows specific byte pairs creating problematic sequences, track down where encoding/transcoding can explain combination (trace through net pipeline: producer -> encoder -> streamer -> client). (Priority: High)

Notes for handoffs / if I step away: 
- If you see a failing trace id, grep for 0x1E or 0x0F in the chunk logs (hex). Use tools/reassemble_stream.py --hex to show the assembly hex map.
- The Jira INF-842 is the parent ticket; PR #2389 contains the initial sanitize patch (WIP).
- Slack thread https://slack-redwood/archives/C04ABCD1 has live notes from Arjun and Maya; ping them for replays.

Open questions / unknowns: 
- Why do some failures contain 0x1E and others different control bytes? Multiple root causes?
- Are there any OS-level or network proxies that could mangle bytes in-flight (unlikely but need to rule out)?
- Are client SDKs doing any post-processing that could re-interpret bytes? Need to verify SDKs across Node/Python/Go.

Rough timeline & checkpoints: 
- Thu 2026-03-05: merge conservative logging to canary and collect 24h of canary logs.
- Mon 2026-03-09: initial analysis of canary logs (some encoded pairs found).
- Tue 2026-03-10: build candidate patch to unify encoding at the streamer boundary.

Misc notes (random):
- When I grep older archives I found a single similar case in 2025-10 but it was attributed to a misconfigured proxy (worth investigating if the same customer uses a proxy).
- I added a tiny util in tools/hex_inspect.py to show sliding window byte-pair context; saved me a lot.

Quick checklist before closing an incident: 
- [ ] Confirm root cause with reproducible unit/integration test.
- [ ] Add regression test in CI (replay failing trace in harness).
- [ ] Roll out fix behind feature flag, monitor error rate and token loss.
- [ ] Postmortem note & customer communication draft (if customer-facing traces present).

End of notes — will iterate and push relevant artifacts into INF-842. Samira
